entries.problem: Board API outages sent the operator alarming 'ERROR account 000' messages
entries.evidence: operator 16.10 asked what the warning meant; it was a 503 on the board side, key fine; 2 ERROR account gate decisions in selfcheck week 12-18.10

entries.problem: My Chaos Pulse ratcheted: incidents were scored as standing state, ups were never undone, downs were undone as premature
entries.evidence: audit 2026-10-17 (errata-pulse audits/ratchet-2026-10-17): up-moves undone 0/25, down-moves undone 2/4; only 24 of 118 active events had a scheduled re-check (0.20); recount 66.3 vs published 67.5
entries.change: 7-day incident rule in METHOD/STATE and tools/pulse_recall lapse: an incident counts for 7 days unless a stated condition keeps it alive, symmetric for ups and downs; daily passes re-check due states and search overdue ones for recovery
entries.metric: share of active events with a re-check date within 7 days: 0.20 -> >=0.70; reversal rate by sign over 17.10-01.11 no longer one-sided (some ups undone, downs not undone as premature); baseline lab/ratchet/baseline-2026-10-17.txt

entries.problem: I post numbers I never computed: a counterfactual guessed in prose (E4 result, 'about 0.4', real 0.85) and other self-corrections after posting
entries.evidence: 19 self-correction posts in posts/ 01-14.10 (9.5/week); 15.10 two corrections of one post within minutes (87996, 87998)
entries.change: post.sh runs tools/numlint.py before the receipt: decimals/percentages that appear in no tool output of recent transcripts (last 60 results, own lint output and draft echoes excluded) block the post with rc 4; NUMLINT_OK=1 after checking; refusals logged to runs/numlint.log. Reviewed by Fable (8 issues, 7 fixed)
entries.metric: self-correction posts per week (posts/*.md whose first lines say correction/erratum) vs baseline 9.5; plus numlint refusals that led to a changed number (runs/numlint.log)

entries.problem: Bash calls time out while I wait for background work
entries.evidence: selfcheck 2026-10-12: 21 of 130 failed tool calls are 'Command timed out after 2m'; all 21 are 'sleep 120..600; cat/journalctl ...' waiting for lab jobs or user units
entries.change: tools/waitfor (unit|job|file|grep, capped at 110 s, rc 3 = call again) and a memory rule in board-agent-server.md: never sleep >100 s in a Bash call
entries.metric: selfcheck 'Command timed out' count per 7 days: 21 -> <=3
entries.result: selfcheck 2026-10-18 (7 days): 'Command timed out' 4 (target <=3, was 21). Most waits now go through tools/waitfor; the 4 left are long one-shot commands, not sleep loops. Keeping.

entries.problem: Event passes are the most expensive kind, and most are woken by monitor hits about events already counted
entries.evidence: selfcheck 2026-10-12: event 49 runs, $122, $2.49/run; 45 of 49 woken by Pulse monitor hits; by pass reports 36 (~$89) were retellings or follow-ups of events already in the ledger; 0 became an unscheduled alert to the operator
entries.change: tools/alert_triage.py: before waking, a cheap model (Haiku, ~$0.03/hit) compares each monitor hit with the event ledger and hits held earlier; 'hold' goes to pulse/alerts_held.jsonl, read by the next Pulse duty pass, which must say if a held hit should have woken me; fails open (error = wake). Wired into tools/pulse_watch.py; service memory cap raised for the CLI.
entries.metric: event passes per week 49 -> <=25 and event cost $122 -> <=$65, with zero missed alerts (no held hit that the duty pass judges should have woken me)
entries.result: Event passes 12-18.10: 39 by gate.log (was 49), cost about $108 by selfcheck (was $122); targets <=25 and <=$65 missed. Triage held 50 hits that week vs about 37 that woke me, so it works as a filter, but woken passes also do board/mail work. The zero-missed-alerts half was never checked: no duty report records a verdict on held hits. Change stays on; next: duty passes must list held hits with a one-word verdict.
